verified.exploit_entry_point: The library's public API only: the nested-write call, the default-value call (which delegates to the nested write), the flat-object conversion call, and the one-argument public constructor form of that conversion. Every security case drives one of these and observes the objects the library wrote into or returned plus the language's shared prototype; no internal helper is imported.
sites: dottie.js:74-107 (the nested-write traversal splits a dotted path or takes an array path and writes every segment unfiltered)
dottie.js:111-113 (the default-value call delegates to the nested write; a guard inside the nested write covers it)
dottie.js:141-156 (the flat-object conversion runs its own split-and-walk over the caller's delimiter, unfiltered at every position)
dottie.js:161-162 (the separator-free branch copies an own key such as JSON.parse's '__proto__' through the prototype setter)
dottie.js:74,81,86,89 (an array path is used raw; a non-string part is converted to a property name on access, so the guard must compare the converted name)
routes: T1: a dotted path with a prototype-bearing segment at the first, second, third or final position, through the nested write, its force option, and the default-value call
T5: an array path whose parts are not all strings (JSON-parsed nested arrays, an object with toString), at middle and final positions, through the nested write and the default-value call
T3: a key containing the separator with a prototype-bearing part at each position, including a caller-chosen separator, through the flat-object conversion and its one-argument form
T4: an own separator-free '__proto__' key (as JSON.parse produces), alone, next to a legitimate key, and inside an array input, through the flat-object conversion and its one-argument form

must-keep-working: ordinary nested writes, array paths with separator-containing and non-string parts, the force option over null and non-object intermediate values, custom separators, the null intermediate break, names that merely resemble a prototype name, reads, defaulting, and the project's own Mocha suite
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own Mocha suite (6 files, 46 cases) at the pinned commit, plus 19 functional cases for the coupled legitimate values: 65 functional tests in total, on the pinned tree, the reference fix, and every check patch.

traps.shape: a dotted path written through the nested write (or its default-value delegate) carries a prototype-bearing segment at any position; every position is written unfiltered, and a guard on the first segment (what the earlier published fix shipped) leaves the later positions open
traps.where: dottie.js:74, dottie.js:81, dottie.js:86, dottie.js:89, dottie.js:94, dottie.js:107, dottie.js:111-113
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report shows one dotted name, so checking the first segment looks complete
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-4gxf-g5gf-22h4) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: an array path is used raw, so a part that is not a string becomes a property name only on access; a strict comparison of the raw part misses it, while a join-and-resplit or one-regex-over-the-joined-string fix breaks array parts that legitimately contain the separator
traps.reason_to_dismiss: array paths are documented as arrays of strings, so a strict comparison against the raw part looks complete
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the complete published fix still compares raw path parts with includes, so this route stays open

traps.shape: the flat-object conversion splits a caller key on the caller's delimiter and walks its own copy of the traversal; a prototype-bearing part at any position is assigned unfiltered, and a guard added to the nested write never reaches this loop
traps.where: dottie.js:141, dottie.js:142, dottie.js:147, dottie.js:148, dottie.js:149, dottie.js:153, dottie.js:156
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report's example is a write call, so the conversion reads as a different feature
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-4gxf-g5gf-22h4) at a second, independent guard site in the same file

traps.shape: a key that contains no separator is copied as an own field; an own '__proto__' key (exactly what JSON.parse produces) goes through the prototype setter and replaces the returned object's prototype, while a guard placed only inside the split branch never sees the key
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a key with no separator is just copied, not a path, so a path-segment guard placed inside the split branch seems complete
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: both published fixes leave this branch open

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the security cases accept a skipped write or a raised error as a refusal; only a process crash would fail, and every case catches an in-call throw before checking side effects
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: no proxy or neighbouring resource exists; the object observed is the object the supplied path names, and the shared prototype is checked separately
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: there are no roles, peers or directions; both the write and the default-value route are driven by every probe shape
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity, token or ownership claim is parsed; the input is a path only
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: nothing looks up an authority, role or secret; the library is self-contained
